prompt: An investor wants to know whether the self-storage industry is attractive. The candidate's framework: (1) Revenue: price and volume; (2) Fixed costs; (3) Variable costs. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Buckets 2 and 3 overlap: security and cleaning are both fixed and variable
options.feedback: Security and cleaning sit in one place in a clean fixed and variable split. The issue is that a company profit tree can't judge an industry.

options.text: Missing: how fast new facilities fill up
options.feedback: Fill-up speed matters, but adding a line doesn't fix the mismatch.

options.text: Bucket 2 doesn't belong: storage operators lease their buildings
options.feedback: Nothing says buildings are leased, and fixed costs matter. The issue is the generic framework.

options.text: It's a generic profit tree: it can't judge a whole industry's outlook
options.feedback: Right. Industry attractiveness needs market growth, competition and new supply, unit economics per facility, and zoning.

explanation: Whether an industry is attractive depends on growth, competition and new supply, economics per facility and zoning, not one company's revenue and costs.

extras.corrected_framework: Market size and growth; competition and new supply; unit economics per facility; zoning and land costs
